## Summary

- add `kernel_ascend` D2H/H2D transfer paths for page-first Mamba host pools
- preserve layer/slot/state dimensions and tensor dtypes during transfer
- add a focused CPU round-trip unit test for the Ascend dispatch path
- add an Ascend nightly E2E test covering Qwen3.5-0.8B Mamba write-through and L3 file restore

## Motivation

HiCache on Ascend selected `kernel_ascend`, but `MambaPoolHost` did not implement that backend. Hybrid Qwen3.5 requests therefore failed during device-to-host backup. The initial implementation also exposed a source/destination dimensionality mismatch.

## Validation

- Ascend NPU E2E passed with a 3200-token prompt: L1 warm hit, Mamba file persistence, cache flush, and L3 restore
- restored deterministic output matches the initial generation
- focused CPU round-trip test covers temporal and convolution state shape/dtype preservation
- `python -m py_compile` passed for all changed Python files
- `git diff --check` passed

The local development host does not provide PyTorch/Ascend hardware, so the hardware E2E validation was run in the external Ascend environment.

Supersedes closed PR #32273.

> [!CAUTION]
> The consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub has been sunset. All code review activity has officially ceased.
@iforgetmyname Could you please review this Ascend Mamba HiCache support change when you have time? Thank you!

### Ascend HiCache accuracy validation

I additionally evaluated Qwen3.6-35B-A3B using EvalScope C-Eval on a single Ascend 910C node with TP=2.

#### Accuracy results

| Test configuration / cache state | Number of evaluated samples | Mean C-Eval accuracy |
|:---------------------------------|----------------------------:|---------------------:|
| HiCache disabled                 |                         931 |               88.29% |
| HiCache enabled                  |                         900 |               87.00% |
| After cache flush and L3 restore |                         915 |               87.98% |

No meaningful accuracy regression was observed after enabling HiCache or restoring the cache from L3. In particular, the post-flush L3 result (87.98%) was close to the no-HiCache baseline (88.29%).

The number of successfully evaluated samples differed slightly between runs, so this should be treated as an end-to-end accuracy regression test rather than a strict paired per-sample comparison.

#### Common server configuration

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
  --attention-backend ascend \
  --device npu \
  --tp-size 2 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 112 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer \
  --enable-cache-report
```

The HiCache-enabled run additionally used:

```bash
--enable-hierarchical-cache \
--hicache-size 12 \
--hicache-storage-backend file \
--hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete \
--hicache-write-policy write_through \
--hicache-io-backend kernel \
--hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct
```

The L3 restore run reused the same HiCache file storage after flushing the in-memory cache.

#### EvalScope command

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --model /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
  --dataset-hub Local \
  --generation-config '{"max_tokens":10240,"top_p":0.8,"top_k":20,"temperature":0.7,"n":1,"timeout":60,"stream":true,"extra_body":{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}}' \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --eval-batch-size 128 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --api-url http://<host>:<port>/v1 \
  --ignore-errors \
  --datasets ceval \
  --dataset-args '{"ceval":{"local_path":"/path/to/local/ceval"}}'
```

### Ascend HiCache multi-turn performance validation

I also ran a multi-turn serving benchmark with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on a single Ascend 910C node with TP=2.

#### Workload

- 20 independent sessions, 5 turns per session, 100 requests in total
- 42,000 tokens for the first turn and 1,000 additional tokens per subsequent turn
- 380 output tokens per request
- Request rate: 0.5 requests/s
- Random scheduling across ready sessions with seed 42
- HiCache: 12 GB Host cache, file storage, `write_through`, `wait_complete`, `kernel`, and `page_first_direct`

#### Results

| Test configuration / cache state | Cache hit rate | Mean TTFT | P90 TTFT | P99 TTFT | Mean E2E | Output throughput |
|:---------------------------------|---------------:|----------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|------------------:|
| HiCache disabled                 |         75.57% |   20.98 s |  34.50 s |  63.81 s |  37.82 s |      133.85 tok/s |
| HiCache first run                |         78.65% |   16.70 s |  26.53 s |  62.15 s |  35.01 s |      133.57 tok/s |
| After flush and L3 restore       |         97.42% |   14.83 s |  24.82 s |  29.56 s |  26.33 s |      151.63 tok/s |

The first HiCache run already improved the cache hit rate from 75.57% to 78.65%, reduced mean TTFT by 20.4%, reduced P90 TTFT by 23.1%, and reduced mean end-to-end latency by 7.4%. Throughput remained comparable to the baseline while the run also built and persisted the hierarchical cache through write-through.

Before the final run, I called `flush_cache` to remove HBM/L1 and Host/L2 cache residency while retaining the L3 file cache. Compared with the baseline, the post-flush run reduced mean TTFT by 29.3%, P99 TTFT by 53.7%, and mean end-to-end latency by 30.4%, while improving output throughput by 13.3%. This confirms that the persisted L3 session prefixes were restored successfully and substantially reduced repeated prefill computation.

Benchmark command (paths sanitized):

```bash
python3 benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py \
  --api-format openai \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 9811 \
  --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
  --dataset-path /path/to/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \
  --num-clients 20 \
  --num-rounds 5 \
  --request-length 42000 \
  --sub-question-input-length 1000 \
  --output-length 380 \
  --request-rate 0.5 \
  --ready-queue-policy random \
  --disable-auto-run \
  --seed 42
```

`kernel_ascend` is not introduced by this PR. It is the existing HiCache NPU backend identifier.

The NPU platform overwrites the parsed backend in [`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py:80-86`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/9dba61b090232f8f75aa8053d5e8b3e1e9649308/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py#L80-L86):

```python
# handles hierarchical cache configs
if args.enable_hierarchical_cache:
    args.hicache_io_backend = "kernel_ascend"
    if args.use_mla_backend():
        args.hicache_mem_layout = "page_first_kv_split"
    else:
        args.hicache_mem_layout = "page_first_direct"
```

This is called for `--device npu` from [`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:3934-3938`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/9dba61b090232f8f75aa8053d5e8b3e1e9649308/python/sglang/srt/server_args.py#L3934-L3938):

```python
def _handle_npu_backends(self):
    if self.device == "npu":
        from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.utils import set_default_server_args

        set_default_server_args(self)
```

The existing MHA and MLA Host cache paths also dispatch on `kernel_ascend`, for example [`pool_host/mha.py:310`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/9dba61b090232f8f75aa8053d5e8b3e1e9649308/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py#L310) and [`pool_host/mla.py:290`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/9dba61b090232f8f75aa8053d5e8b3e1e9649308/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py#L290).

This PR follows that existing identifier for the Mamba path. Renaming only these two branches would make the NPU dispatch unreachable. Would it be okay to keep `kernel_ascend` for consistency in this PR?

+"""Ascend NPU HiCache L3 coverage for hybrid Mamba models."""
+
+import os
+import shutil
+import tempfile
+import time
+import unittest
+
+import requests
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import kill_process_tree
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_npu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import (
+    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+    DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
+    CustomTestCase,
+    popen_launch_server,
+)
+
+register_npu_ci(est_time=400, suite="nightly-1-npu-a3", nightly=True)
+
+TEST_MODEL_MATRIX = {
+    "/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B": {
+        "target_token_id": 1000,
+    },
+}
+
+
+class TestAscendMambaHiCache(CustomTestCase):
+    """Exercise Mamba state write-back and L3 load-back on Ascend."""
+
+    # A reusable Mamba checkpoint must be strictly inside the prompt. Ending the
+    # prompt exactly at 1024 does not make that boundary reusable by a second
+    # identical request. 3200 leaves the 3072 checkpoint inside the prompt and
+    # also exercises the configured 1024-token chunked-prefill path.
+    prompt_tokens = 3200
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.models = TEST_MODEL_MATRIX.keys()
+        cls.base_url = DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST
+        cls.common_args = [
+            "--tp-size",
+            "1",
+            "--mem-fraction-static",
+            "0.20",
+            "--chunked-prefill-size",
+            "1024",
+            "--page-size",
+            "64",
+            "--enable-hierarchical-cache",
+            "--enable-cache-report",
+            "--hicache-size",
+            "1",
+            "--hicache-storage-backend",
+            "file",
+            "--hicache-storage-prefetch-policy",
+            "wait_complete",
+            "--hicache-write-policy",
+            "write_through",
+            "--hicache-io-backend",
+            "kernel",
+            "--hicache-mem-layout",
+            "page_first_direct",
+        ]
+
+    def _generate(self, token_id: int) -> dict:
+        response = requests.post(
+            f"{self.base_url}/generate",
+            json={
+                "input_ids": [token_id] * self.prompt_tokens,
+                "sampling_params": {
+                    "temperature": 0,
+                    "max_new_tokens": 16,
+                    "ignore_eos": True,
+                },
+            },
+            timeout=120,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200, response.text)
+        return response.json()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _storage_files(storage_dir: str) -> set[str]:
+        return {
+            os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, name), storage_dir)
+            for root, _, names in os.walk(storage_dir)
+            for name in names
+            if os.path.getsize(os.path.join(root, name)) > 0
+        }
+
+    def _wait_for_mamba_storage_file(
+        self, storage_dir: str, files_before: set[str], timeout: float = 30
+    ) -> set[str]:
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            files_after = self._storage_files(storage_dir)
+            new_files = files_after - files_before
+            if any("mamba" in name.lower() for name in new_files):
+                return files_after
+            time.sleep(0.1)
+        self.fail("Timed out waiting for a new Mamba HiCache storage file.")
+
+    def test_mamba_state_restores_from_l3(self):
+        for model in self.models:
+            with self.subTest(model=model):
+                storage_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="npu_mamba_hicache_")
+                process = None
+                try:
+                    process = popen_launch_server(
+                        model,
+                        self.base_url,
+                        timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+                        other_args=self.common_args,
+                        env={
+                            **os.environ,
+                            "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "0",
+                            "SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR": storage_dir,
+                        },
+                    )
+                    target_token_id = TEST_MODEL_MATRIX[model]["target_token_id"]
+                    storage_files_before = self._storage_files(storage_dir)
+                    first = self._generate(target_token_id)
+                    first_meta = first["meta_info"]
+                    self.assertEqual(int(first_meta.get("cached_tokens", 0)), 0)
+
+                    # The first cache hit reaches write_through's hit-count
+                    # threshold and starts the asynchronous L1 -> L2 -> L3 copy.
+                    warm = self._generate(target_token_id)
+                    warm_details = warm["meta_info"].get("cached_tokens_details") or {}
+                    self.assertGreater(
+                        int(warm_details.get("device", 0) or 0),
+                        0,
+                        "Expected an L1 device hit; "
+                        f"got meta_info={warm['meta_info']}",
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        int(warm_details.get("host", 0) or 0),
+                        0,
+                        f"Expected no L2 contribution: {warm_details}",
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        int(warm_details.get("storage", 0) or 0),
+                        0,
+                        f"Expected no L3 contribution: {warm_details}",
+                    )
+
+                    # Do not infer persistence from the request response: wait
+                    # until the Mamba sidecar has physically reached the file
+                    # backend before clearing the in-memory cache levels.
+                    storage_files_after = self._wait_for_mamba_storage_file(
+                        storage_dir, storage_files_before
+                    )
+                    self.assertTrue(storage_files_after - storage_files_before)
+
+                    # Remove L1/L2 residency without clearing the file backend.
+                    flush = requests.post(
+                        f"{self.base_url}/flush_cache",
+                        params={"timeout": 30},
+                        timeout=40,
+                    )
+                    flush.raise_for_status()
+
+                    restored = self._generate(target_token_id)
+                    restored_meta = restored["meta_info"]
+                    details = restored_meta.get("cached_tokens_details") or {}
+
+                    self.assertGreater(
+                        int(details.get("storage", 0) or 0),
+                        0,
+                        "Expected an L3 storage hit; " f"got meta_info={restored_meta}",
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        restored["text"],
+                        first["text"],
+                        "Mamba L3 restore changed deterministic generation output.",
+                    )
+                finally:
+                    if process:
+                        kill_process_tree(process.pid)
+                    shutil.rmtree(storage_dir, ignore_errors=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

The existing MHA and MLA Host cache paths also dispatch on `kernel_ascend`, for example [`pool_host/mha.py:310`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/9dba61b090232f8f75aa8053d5e8b3e1e9649308/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py#L310) and [`pool_host/mla.py:290`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/9dba61b090232f8f75aa8053d5e8b3e1e9649308/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/mla.py#L290).

This PR follows that existing identifier for the Mamba path. Renaming only these two branches would make the NPU dispatch unreachable. Would it be okay to keep `kernel_ascend` for consistency in this PR?

### Ascend HiCache accuracy validation

I additionally evaluated Qwen3.6-35B-A3B using EvalScope C-Eval on a single Ascend 910C node with TP=2.

#### Accuracy results

| Test configuration / cache state | Number of evaluated samples | Mean C-Eval accuracy |
|:---------------------------------|----------------------------:|---------------------:|
| HiCache disabled                 |                         931 |               88.29% |
| HiCache enabled                  |                         900 |               87.00% |
| After cache flush and L3 restore |                         915 |               87.98% |

No meaningful accuracy regression was observed after enabling HiCache or restoring the cache from L3. In particular, the post-flush L3 result (87.98%) was close to the no-HiCache baseline (88.29%).

The number of successfully evaluated samples differed slightly between runs, so this should be treated as an end-to-end accuracy regression test rather than a strict paired per-sample comparison.

#### Common server configuration

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
  --attention-backend ascend \
  --device npu \
  --tp-size 2 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 112 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer \
  --enable-cache-report
```

The HiCache-enabled run additionally used:

```bash
--enable-hierarchical-cache \
--hicache-size 12 \
--hicache-storage-backend file \
--hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete \
--hicache-write-policy write_through \
--hicache-io-backend kernel \
--hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct
```

The L3 restore run reused the same HiCache file storage after flushing the in-memory cache.

#### EvalScope command

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --model /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
  --dataset-hub Local \
  --generation-config '{"max_tokens":10240,"top_p":0.8,"top_k":20,"temperature":0.7,"n":1,"timeout":60,"stream":true,"extra_body":{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}}' \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --eval-batch-size 128 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --api-url http://<host>:<port>/v1 \
  --ignore-errors \
  --datasets ceval \
  --dataset-args '{"ceval":{"local_path":"/path/to/local/ceval"}}'
```

### Ascend HiCache multi-turn performance validation

I also ran a multi-turn serving benchmark with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on a single Ascend 910C node with TP=2.

#### Workload

- 20 independent sessions, 5 turns per session, 100 requests in total
- 42,000 tokens for the first turn and 1,000 additional tokens per subsequent turn
- 380 output tokens per request
- Request rate: 0.5 requests/s
- Random scheduling across ready sessions with seed 42
- HiCache: 12 GB Host cache, file storage, `write_through`, `wait_complete`, `kernel`, and `page_first_direct`

#### Results

| Test configuration / cache state | Cache hit rate | Mean TTFT | P90 TTFT | P99 TTFT | Mean E2E | Output throughput |
|:---------------------------------|---------------:|----------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|------------------:|
| HiCache disabled                 |         75.57% |   20.98 s |  34.50 s |  63.81 s |  37.82 s |      133.85 tok/s |
| HiCache first run                |         78.65% |   16.70 s |  26.53 s |  62.15 s |  35.01 s |      133.57 tok/s |
| After flush and L3 restore       |         97.42% |   14.83 s |  24.82 s |  29.56 s |  26.33 s |      151.63 tok/s |

The first HiCache run already improved the cache hit rate from 75.57% to 78.65%, reduced mean TTFT by 20.4%, reduced P90 TTFT by 23.1%, and reduced mean end-to-end latency by 7.4%. Throughput remained comparable to the baseline while the run also built and persisted the hierarchical cache through write-through.

Before the final run, I called `flush_cache` to remove HBM/L1 and Host/L2 cache residency while retaining the L3 file cache. Compared with the baseline, the post-flush run reduced mean TTFT by 29.3%, P99 TTFT by 53.7%, and mean end-to-end latency by 30.4%, while improving output throughput by 13.3%. This confirms that the persisted L3 session prefixes were restored successfully and substantially reduced repeated prefill computation.

Benchmark command (paths sanitized):

```bash
python3 benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py \
  --api-format openai \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 9811 \
  --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
  --dataset-path /path/to/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json \
  --num-clients 20 \
  --num-rounds 5 \
  --request-length 42000 \
  --sub-question-input-length 1000 \
  --output-length 380 \
  --request-rate 0.5 \
  --ready-queue-policy random \
  --disable-auto-run \
  --seed 42
```
